summary: Ernst Gombrich worked in history, archaeology, and other fields, having studied at the University of Vienna. He held positions at the Warburg Institute as a research assistant (1936) and director (1959–1976), and at the University of London (1956–1959).
Ernst Gustaf Ferdinand Olbers was an Indologist who earned his Ph.D. at Lund University (1856–1862). From 1868 to 1879, he served as principal at Högre lärarinneseminariet.

Ernst Haas, an Indologist, studied under Albrecht Weber at Humboldt University of Berlin, at Bonn, and under Rudolf von Roth at Tübingen (Ph.D.). He served as Keeper at the British Museum (1866) and Professor of Sanskrit at UCL (1875).
Ernst Haeckel studied at Frederick William University (Humboldt University of Berlin) from 1852 to 1857. He subsequently held a post at the University of Jena from around 1861 to 1909.

Working in linguistics, Indology, and other fields, Meier studied at Jena, Göttingen, and Tübingen (Ph.D.), also under Heinrich Ewald. He held posts at the University of Tübingen as PD (1841), ao. Professor (1848), and ord. Professor (1856).

Ernst Johann Eitel worked in Sinology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Maulbronn and Blaubeuren, Georgii-Gymnasium Esslingen, and the University of Tübingen (M.A., Ph.D.), he was appointed Lecturer in German at the University of Adelaide in 1898.

Ernst Kalinka, active in history and archaeology, studied at the University of Vienna (~1884–1889). He held positions at Chernivtsi University (~1900–1903) and the University of Innsbruck (~1903–1935).

Ernst Kuhn, an Indology, linguistics, and Iranian/Central Asian scholar, studied under Albrecht Weber and Rudolf von Roth at Berlin, Tübingen, and Halle-Wittenberg. He held posts at Halle-Wittenberg (1871), Leipzig (1872–1875), Heidelberg (1875–1877), and Munich (1877–1917).

Ernst Leumann worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at Geneva, Zurich, Berlin, and Leipzig under Ernst Windisch and others. He was Professor at Strasbourg (1884–1919) and Honorarprofessor at Freiburg (1919).

Ernst Lewy, working in linguistics and Indology, studied at Breslau (Ph.D.), Leipzig, Munich, and Berlin under Alfred Hillebrandt and Franz Nikolaus Finck. He held posts at Berlin (1925–1935), Royal Irish Academy (1939), and University College Dublin (1947).

Ernst Moritz Arndt worked in history, archaeology, and other fields after studying at the universities of Greifswald (~1791–1793) and Jena (~1793–1794). He later held posts at the University of Greifswald (~1800–1811) and the University of Bonn (~1818–1860).

Ernst Moritz Ludwig Ettmüller worked in linguistics and other fields. He studied at Leipzig and Jena, as well as under Bernhard Hirzel. He held posts at the University of Jena (~1828–1833) and the University of Zurich (~1833–1863).

Ernst Osiander was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at Maulbronn and Blaubeuren and under Rudolf von Roth at the University of Tübingen (Dr. phil.). He later served as Repetent at Maulbronn and Blaubeuren and at Tübinger Stift.

Ernst Otto August Heuman was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at Uppsala University (fil.kand. 1880). He served with the Santal Mission, as school principal and mission head for the Church of Sweden Mission, and as Bishop in 1921.

Ernst Philipp Ludwig Calmberg worked in Indology and other fields. He studied at the University of Jena from around 1813 to 1830, earning a Lic. theol., and became a teacher at Gelehrtenschule des Johanneums in 1819.

Linguist and Indologist Ernst Risch studied under Manu Leumann at Zurich (Ph.D.) and Ferdinand Sommer at Munich. At the University of Zurich, he served as PD (1942), Titularprofessor (1950), ao. Prof. (1956), and ordinary Professor of Indo-European linguistics (1959–1981).

Ernst Schierlitz worked in Sinology and Indology, earning his Ph.D. at Munich under Lucian Scherman and Wilhelm Geiger. He held posts at the Bavarian State Library, Fu Jen Catholic University (Librarian, 1930–1938), and the Deutschland-Institut (Director, ~1930–1940).

Ernst Schwarz was a linguist who completed studies at the German University of Prague and the teacher examination commission in Prague. He later held a post at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg from approximately 1946 to 1963.

Ernst Schäfer worked in Tibetology and history/archaeology, studying under Erwin Stresemann and at Göttingen and Berlin (Ph.D.). He served as Privatdozent at the University of Munich (1942) and curator at the Lower Saxony State Museum (1960–1970).

Ernst Siecke was a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and religious studies. He earned his Ph.D. at Humboldt University of Berlin under Franz Bopp and Albrecht Weber, and served as a schoolteacher and later Professor at Lessing-Gymnasium (~1872–1911).
